title: Draw ToPickup and ToScore
summary: Draw and generate the two Choreo paths, with the exact names and places the routine needs.

say.never:
The autonomous routine drives two **paths** you draw in Choreo. **ToPickup** goes from the start spot to the game piece. **ToScore** carries on from the game piece to the scoring spot.

You will do five things: 1) set the robot up in Choreo, 2) draw ToPickup with a start, a point in the middle and an end, 3) name it exactly and press Generate, 4) draw ToScore so that it starts where ToPickup ended, 5) name it and generate it.

You are done when both paths are drawn, named exactly, and go where they should. Verify checks this. This lesson uses the Choreo pane just like the **Choreo** lesson, so do that one first if the editor is new to you.
say.bit: Set Choreo's drive type to Differential, then draw two paths, ToPickup and ToScore, with exact names, and generate each. ToScore must start where ToPickup ends.

say.never: Before you draw anything, the Choreo pane needs this robot's settings. Choreo starts with its own defaults, and the main one is wrong for us: **Drive Type** is **Swerve**, but this robot is **Differential** (two sides of wheels, like a tank). If it stays Swerve, Choreo makes Swerve paths, the follower cannot use them and Verify says so. The other numbers (mass, wheel size and so on) should match this robot too, or a path may ask for more than the robot can do.
say.bit: Before drawing: set Drive Type to Differential and the robot numbers in Choreo's Document Settings.

say.never: Click the menu, the three-line icon at the top left of the Choreo pane next to the Choreo title, then choose **Document Settings** and open the **Robot Config** tab. Click **I did it** when you can see Drive Type.
say.bit: Menu (three lines, top left), Document Settings, Robot Config tab.

waitFor.hint: open the menu, then Document Settings and Robot Config, then click I did it.

say.never: Slide **Drive Type** from Swerve to **Differential**. Set **Trackwidth** to **24** in. Click **I did it** when Drive Type reads Differential.
say.bit: Drive Type to Differential, Trackwidth 24 in.

waitFor.hint: set Drive Type to Differential and Trackwidth to 24 in, then click I did it.

say.never: Type these, pressing **Enter** after each: Mass **50** kg, MOI **7.5** kg m^2, Bumpers **17** in (front, back and sides), Wheel Radius **3** in, Motor Rev / Wheel Rev **8.45**, Motor Max Speed **6000** RPM, Motor Max Torque **1.0** N*m, Wheel COF **1.5**. Click **I did it** when they match, then close the dialog.
say.bit: Mass 50, MOI 7.5, Bumpers 17, Wheel Radius 3, gearing 8.45, 6000 RPM, 1.0 N*m, COF 1.5.

waitFor.hint: type the robot numbers, then click I did it.

say.never:
The project already knows four places, saved as **named poses**: `Start`, `Pickup`, `ScoreSpot` and `Goal`. Your two paths use three of them. The numbers are on the board, in meters and degrees.

The robot is standing on Pickup when ToScore begins, so **ToScore must start at Pickup**: the same spot as ToPickup's last waypoint. The check allows only a few centimeters of gap.
say.bit: ToPickup: Start to Pickup. ToScore: Pickup to ScoreSpot. The two paths must meet at Pickup.

board.code:
Start      x 1.5   y 1.5   heading 0
Pickup     x 5.5   y 2.5   heading 0
ScoreSpot  x 6.5   y 5.0   heading 90

say.never:
A path is a list of **waypoints**, and the order in the list is the order the robot drives. A **Pose Waypoint** pins where the robot is and which way it faces. A **Translation Waypoint** pins only the position and lets Choreo choose the heading. A path needs at least three: a start, a point to steer through, an end.

The **name** matters most of all: your Java loads each path by its name, so the spelling and capital letters must be exact. Rename it in the Choreo pane, not by renaming the file. Then press **Generate**: Choreo works out the schedule and saves the file.
say.bit: Pose waypoint = position and heading, translation waypoint = position only. Order in the list is the driving order. Names must match your Java exactly. Generate saves the path.

say.never: Press the **+** in the paths list to make a new path.
say.bit: Press **+** to add a path.

say.never: Click the path's name in the list and type `ToPickup`, then press **Enter**. The spelling and capital letters must be exact, because your Java will load the path by this name. Rename it in the Choreo pane, not by renaming the file. Click **I did it** when it says ToPickup.
say.bit: Rename the path to exactly `ToPickup` (capital T and P).

waitFor.hint: name the path ToPickup, then click I did it.

say.never: Pick the **Pose Waypoint** tool (it pins where the robot is and which way it faces), then click the field to drop the first waypoint. Anywhere is fine for now, you will type the exact numbers next.
say.bit: Choose Pose Waypoint and click the field once for the start.

waitFor.hint: pick Pose Waypoint and click the field.

say.never: Click the waypoint in the list on the left. Its numbers appear in a panel: type **1.5** in the X box, **1.5** in the Y box and **0** degrees for the heading, pressing **Enter** after each. Click **I did it** when the waypoint sits on the Start spot.

waitFor.hint: set the waypoint to 1.5, 1.5, heading 0, then click I did it.

say.never: Pick the **Translation Waypoint** tool and click the field between the two ends. It pins only the position and lets Choreo pick the heading. A path needs at least three waypoints: a start, a point to steer through, an end.
say.bit: Add a Translation Waypoint between start and end.

waitFor.hint: pick Translation Waypoint and click the field.

say.never: Click it in the list and type X **3.5** and Y **2.0**. Any spot between the ends works, this one just makes a gentle curve. Click **I did it** when it is set.
say.bit: Set the middle waypoint to x 3.5, y 2.0.

say.never: Back to the **Pose Waypoint** tool, and click the field once more for the end of the path. The order in the list is the order the robot drives.
say.bit: Choose Pose Waypoint and click once more for the end.

waitFor.hint: pick Pose Waypoint and click the field again.

say.never: Click the last waypoint and type X **5.5**, Y **2.5**, heading **0** degrees. Click **I did it** when it sits on Pickup.
say.bit: Set the last waypoint to x 5.5, y 2.5, heading 0 degrees.

waitFor.hint: set the end waypoint to 5.5, 2.5, heading 0, then click I did it.

say.never: A speed limit keeps the robot gentle, so the follower can keep up. Pick **Max Velocity**, click the first and last waypoints (it shows in the list as **Max Velo**), then set it to **1.8** m/s. The Choreo lesson showed this. Click **I did it** (or just skip it).
say.bit: Optional: a Max Velocity of 1.8 m/s on the whole path. Click I did it to move on.

waitFor.hint: add the optional Max Velocity, or just click I did it.

say.never: Press **Generate** to make Choreo work out the schedule and save the file. Watch the path appear on the field. If it fails, a waypoint or limit is probably impossible, see the "When a path won't generate" guide in the Choreo lesson. Click **I did it** when the path is drawn.
say.bit: Press Generate and watch the path appear.

waitFor.hint: press Generate and wait for the path, then click I did it.

say.never:
ToScore is drawn the same way, with one rule: its first waypoint sits exactly on Pickup, where ToPickup ended. Its end is the scoring spot, and the heading turns to face roughly the goal.

If you capped ToPickup's speed, cap this one the same so the follower can keep up. The name must be exactly `ToScore`.
say.bit: ToScore starts on Pickup and ends on ScoreSpot. Same speed cap, exact name.

steps.title: Add the second path and name it

say.never: Press **+** again for a second path, then rename it to exactly `ToScore`: click its name, type it, press **Enter**.
say.bit: Press **+** again and name it exactly `ToScore`.

say.never: The robot is standing on Pickup when ToScore begins, so ToScore must **start at Pickup**: the same spot as ToPickup's last waypoint. The check allows only a few centimeters of gap. Make three waypoints: a **pose** at the start, a **translation** in the middle, a **pose** at the end.
say.bit: ToScore starts on Pickup, where ToPickup ended. Pose, translation, pose.

waitFor.hint: drop three waypoints: pose, translation, pose.

say.never: Click each waypoint in the list and type its numbers. First: X **5.5**, Y **2.5**, heading **0**. Middle: X **6.0**, Y **3.8**. Last: X **6.5**, Y **5.0**, heading **90** degrees (about 1.57 if Choreo asks in radians). Click **I did it** when all three are typed.
say.bit: First 5.5, 2.5 at 0 degrees. Middle 6.0, 3.8. Last 6.5, 5.0 at 90 degrees.

waitFor.hint: type the three waypoints, then click I did it.

say.never: If you capped ToPickup, add **Max Velocity** 1.8 m/s here too. Then press **Generate** again for this path. Click **I did it** when ToScore has drawn.
say.bit: Optional Max Velocity 1.8, then Generate ToScore.

waitFor.hint: generate ToScore, then click I did it.

say.never: Open the lesson chip and press **Verify**. **Two paths drawn** and **Paths go where they should** should pass now. **Paths named ToPickup and ToScore** also looks at your Java (`Autos.java` has to load them by name), so it passes after the next guide.
say.bit: Press Verify. The naming check also reads your Java, so it passes after the next guide.
